summary: FireTrust is a free, browser-based prototype for the challenge “Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots”. MODIS and VIIRS see the ground differently, so their raw fire counts can’t be compared, and a sensor change can look like a fire trend. FireTrust scales VIIRS counts to MODIS-equivalent counts using the years both sensors flew. It then gives every week a trust score showing how closely the sensors agree, and flags unusually busy weeks against the area’s normal season. Results appear as Fire Rings (one ring per year), a trust calendar, a season-shift chart and a share card in English, Hindi and Punjabi. It helps responders, scientists and land managers read fire history with honest uncertainty. Our demo uses synthetic sample data, and the app also accepts real NASA FIRMS files.
details:
What it does. FireTrust harmonizes NASA MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections into one record and shows how much to trust each week. It runs fully in the browser, and no data is uploaded anywhere.

How it works. Detections are counted per day for each sensor. On the days both sensors were flying, the ratio of their totals becomes a scale factor that turns VIIRS counts into MODIS-equivalent counts. Each week gets a trust level based on how close the two scaled counts are and how many 0.25-degree map cells where MODIS saw fire VIIRS also saw. Each week is compared with the same week in other years, and unusually busy weeks are flagged. A season-shift chart tracks the date by which half of a season’s detections have happened.

Views. Fire Rings, a trust calendar, a season-shift chart, a calibration check, and a share card for WhatsApp in English, Hindi and Punjabi.

Benefits and intended impact. It makes the fire record easier to compare across the sensor change and shows its uncertainty. It is meant for responders, scientists, land managers and communities, for example for stubble burning in north India.

Tools. HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript with no libraries, SVG and Canvas, hosted on GitHub Pages. Data source: NASA FIRMS.

Limits. This is a prototype. The calibration is one simple ratio, the trust thresholds are provisional, and satellites only see fires when they pass over. The demo uses synthetic sample data, and no real-world results are claimed.
